answer: An agent economy anchors every identity to a unique sealed replica: each vertex must store two gigabytes of key-specific bytes, re-encrypted so no two accounts can share one copy. Every close the protocol pushes a river of random read challenges, and a vertex that cannot return the exact bytes from its own replica forfeits a five hundred POA bond. One thousand clones must each hold a distinct two gigabyte replica, two terabytes total, rising linearly with n, because the sealing anchor binds the bytes to a single key and nothing deduplicates across the farm.
